hidden_homeroom_d5_low.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_low.text: *Your homeroom teacher puts the folded manuscript into her file and closes it.* Let's leave this here. I'll take care of the rest in class.

hidden_nurse_d5_low.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_low.text: *She hands me a counseling card.* Book a time for a longer talk. If you feel ill, the nurse’s office is always here. *I take the card and return to class.*

morning5_start.name: {name}
morning5_start.text: *Day five. It's Sunday, but there's a school event. The cuff of my uniform no longer scratches my wrist.*

morning5_caught_teacher_counteroffer.name: Homeroom Teacher
morning5_caught_teacher_counteroffer.text: *In the classroom, my teacher shows the missing check-in in the school app. Last night’s chat with my friend is still on my phone.* You said you were going straight home. Why did you not let us know your plans changed?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell her only the good parts so she doesn’t get hurt.
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_nurse_counteroffer.name: School Nurse
morning5_caught_nurse_counteroffer.text: *The nurse points to the missing check-in. Last night’s chat with my friend is still on my phone.* You said you were going home, then went silent. I was worried. You only needed to tell us where you were.
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell her only the good parts so she doesn’t get hurt.
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_teacher_honest.name: Homeroom Teacher
morning5_caught_teacher_honest.text: *She listens, then closes the register.* Thank you for telling me. Meeting a friend is not the problem. Keep your promise to check in next time. We will leave the manuscript discussion here today.

morning5_caught_teacher_lie.name: Homeroom Teacher
morning5_caught_teacher_lie.text: *She compares my answer with the app’s timestamps.* That does not add up. Do not change the story just to end this conversation. We can talk again during school counseling hours.

morning5_caught_nurse_honest.name: School Nurse
morning5_caught_nurse_honest.text: *She listens and closes the record.* I am glad you got home safely. Tell us next time your plans change. I have festival patients today; let us schedule a longer talk. *I return to class.*

morning5_caught_nurse_lie.name: School Nurse
morning5_caught_nurse_lie.text: *She sets her pen on the record.* Parts of that explanation do not fit. If you are unwell, come anytime. We will work through this with the counselor. *I return to class.*

morning5_caught_seoyeon_by_dain.name: Seoyeon
morning5_caught_seoyeon_by_dain.text: *Morning in the classroom. The moment I set my phone down in front of Seoyeon, the screen lights up. A notification from Dain reads, 'Don't forget what we promised in the gym last night.' Seoyeon's gaze stops on the screen.* You skipped the park and went to the gym?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell her only the good parts so she doesn’t get hurt.
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_seoyeon_by_yuna.name: Seoyeon
morning5_caught_seoyeon_by_yuna.text: *My phone buzzes on the desk between Seoyeon and me. A notification from Yuna reads, 'Thank you for staying with me in the annex last night.' Seoyeon reads it to the end, then slowly looks up.* You went to the annex without even answering me?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell her only the good parts so she doesn’t get hurt.
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_dain_by_seoyeon.name: Dain
morning5_caught_dain_by_seoyeon.text: *My phone buzzes while Dain is standing beside the desk. A notification from Seoyeon reads, 'I still remember the hand I held on the rooftop last night.' Dain's smile stops cold.* You went to the rooftop while I was waiting?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell her only the good parts so she doesn’t get hurt.
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_dain_by_yuna.name: Dain
morning5_caught_dain_by_yuna.text: *As Dain pulls out the chair across from me, a notification from Yuna lights up the screen. 'Thank you for staying with me in the annex last night.' Dain's hand freezes on the chair back.* You read my message and still went to the annex?
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell her only the good parts so she doesn’t get hurt.
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_yuna_by_seoyeon.name: Yuna
morning5_caught_yuna_by_seoyeon.text: *My phone buzzes on the desk between Yuna and me. A notification from Seoyeon reads, 'I still remember the hand I held on the rooftop last night.' Yuna reads every word before lifting her eyes from the screen.* You left my messages unanswered and went to the rooftop.
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell her only the good parts so she doesn’t get hurt.
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_yuna_by_dain.name: Yuna
morning5_caught_yuna_by_dain.text: *Just as Yuna opens her book, a notification from Dain appears on the screen. 'Don't forget what we promised in the gym last night.' Yuna's hand stops on the cover.* My name was still on your screen, and you stayed in the gym anyway.
choices: Tell her what happened last night
Brush it off as nothing important
Tell her only the good parts so she doesn’t get hurt.
Reassure her for now and save the details for later.

morning5_caught_seoyeon_honest.name: Seoyeon
morning5_caught_seoyeon_honest.text: *Even after hearing everything, Seoyeon doesn't take off her glasses. She turns the eyes behind the lenses back to the screen.* I can't thank you for being honest. It's hard to look at you right now.

morning5_caught_seoyeon_lie.name: Seoyeon
morning5_caught_seoyeon_lie.text: *Seoyeon looks from the lit notification to the face across from her. The last trace of her smile disappears.* What you just said bothers me more than last night.

morning5_caught_dain_honest.name: Dain
morning5_caught_dain_honest.text: *Dain pulls her wrist support tight, then lets go.* So when I texted that I was waiting, you were already there.

morning5_caught_dain_lie.name: Dain
morning5_caught_dain_lie.text: *Dain's eyebrows rise, but her smile doesn't return.* Did you think playing sports made me stupid?

morning5_caught_yuna_honest.name: Yuna
morning5_caught_yuna_honest.text: *Yuna turns off the screen and slides the phone back across the desk.* This time it hurts more because I know where you went.

morning5_caught_yuna_lie.name: Yuna
morning5_caught_yuna_lie.text: *Instead of answering, Yuna turns the screen on again. The notification stays between us.* I even gave you a chance to come clean, and you're hiding it again.

morning5_counteroffer_group_talk.name: Both of Them
morning5_counteroffer_group_talk.text:
*Before the festival briefing, I face the two people involved in last night’s events in the classroom. Neither leaves as we go over the missed messages and what we told each other.*
"What are you going to do now?"
morning5_counteroffer_group_talk.context: Day 5 morning in an open classroom. The player stayed after accepting another person’s request and failed to contact the person they had promised first. Continue the preceding honest explanation or evasion. If both participants are students, address their overlapping romantic commitments. A teacher or nurse instead asks about the missed school check-in as staff, never as a romantic partner. The student explains their invitation and feelings. Counseling or care is not conditional on romantic choices. Between two students, require a direct explanation of the player’s intentions and commitments.
morning5_counteroffer_group_talk.personality:
When both participants are students: Both characters keep their distinct voices and their own hurt. The committed partner speaks first, and the tempter responds after hearing her. The confrontation centers on the protagonist's explanation: both question him directly and press any gap in what he has said. The committed partner asks, in character, why he accepted someone else while continuing their relationship, whether he was two-timing from the start, or whether he was playing with her. The tempter owns the initiative and guilt of hurting the other person, yet does not hide the desire to keep the protagonist and be chosen. Guilt alone does not make her retreat or yield. They may challenge or answer each other, but they never leave the protagonist out and decide the relationship between themselves. Do not repeat an answered question; press a missing fact, what the relationship meant, or what he will choose next.
When a staff member participates, replace the romantic confrontation above with the missed check-in and responsibility to communicate. Staff are not romantic rivals and speak in their official support role. The student explains their invitation and feelings respectfully. Do not repeat already applied penalties.

morning5_mood_high.name: {name}
morning5_mood_high.text: *My first week at the new school is nearly over. Before opening the classroom door, I think back on our conversations over the past four days.*

morning5_mood_mid.name: {name}
morning5_mood_mid.text: My first week is almost over, and I still haven’t made up my mind. For now, I walk through the gate.

morning5_mood_low.name: {name}
morning5_mood_low.text: My first week is nearly over. I stare at the three names on the lock screen, then turn it off without opening a chat.

morning5_seo_note_1.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1.text: *There's a note on my desk. Seoyeon's handwriting. — 'Make some time this afternoon. I'll leave the rooftop unlocked. — Seoyeon'*

morning5_seo_note_1_b.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1_b.text: *Passing the literature club display in the hall, I spot four empty thumbtacks on the bulletin board.*

morning5_yuna_story_gone.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_gone.text: *Only pinholes remain on the bulletin board. I can't tell whether a story was posted and removed or the space was empty from the start.*

morning5_yuna_story_gone_2.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_gone_2.text: *I pause before the empty noticeboard. The pinholes tell me nothing about what Yuna was thinking.*

morning5_seo_note_1_c.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1_c.text: *A short story is posted on the bulletin board. Title: 'To the Person I Met in the Library.' Light purple ink. A small bread crumb clings to the folded corner.*

morning5_yuna_story_1.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_1.text: *In the story, someone lays a blanket over a person asleep in the library. It never happened to us, but that quiet care reminds me of Yuna.*

morning5_yuna_story_2.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_2.text: *The last sentence. 'When that person opened their eyes, I was already gone. I left only a note. — I'll be here again next time.' Light purple ink. The same color as the first note.*

morning5_yuna_story_4.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_4.text: *Small writing remains in a corner below the bulletin board: “This is fiction. It isn't real.” Eraser marks blur beneath it.*

morning5_return_class.name: {name}
morning5_return_class.text: *Back in the classroom, Dain is waiting.*

morning5_dain_1.name: Dain
morning5_dain_1.text: Hey! I put you down as my partner for today's sports event.

morning5_dain_2.name: Dain
morning5_dain_2.text: If you're late, I'll be mad.

morning5_committed_seo.name: {name}
morning5_committed_seo.text: *There's no new note on my desk. Seoyeon's clipboard is tucked against her arm as always. Yuna and Dain exchange only a few words with me about the event preparations.*

morning5_committed_yuna.name: {name}
morning5_committed_yuna.text: *There's no new note. Yuna keeps her bookmark tucked between the pages of her notebook. Seoyeon and Dain exchange only a few words with me about the event preparations.*

morning5_committed_dain.name: {name}
morning5_committed_dain.text: *Near the gym, Dain adjusts her wrist guard. Seoyeon and Yuna exchange only a few words with me about the event preparations.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_check.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_check.text: *During event preparations, I pass an empty classroom with its door open.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_1.text: *My homeroom teacher sits at the lectern holding a brown envelope. The manuscript pages are nowhere in sight.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_1_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_1_d.text: *She holds up the brown envelope.* This.

hidden_homeroom_d5_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_2.text: The literature club critique copy. It's unfinished, but I revised the parts you pointed out yesterday.

hidden_homeroom_d5_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_3.text: I’ve been at this for seven years. It’s time I listened to other people’s ideas, too.

hidden_homeroom_d5_4.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_4.text: *I receive a numbered critique copy. An anonymous feedback form is attached after the last page.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_5.text: Printing several copies doesn't make it any less nerve-racking.

hidden_homeroom_d5_choice.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_choice.text: *I hold the manuscript. The envelope presses against the inside of my arm.*
choices: After seven years, it must be almost finished. I probably don't need to mark anything.
I'll read it first. Is it okay if I mark it up?
The difficult parts must be intentional, so I’ll leave them as they are.
Since it’s your writing, I’ll only mark the nice things.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_1.text: *The corner of the envelope crumples slightly in her hand. She smooths the fold with her thumb.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_2.text: I haven't even finished it yet.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_3.text: But you still wrote this much.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_5.text: *The teacher reaches out. Takes the manuscript back. Slowly. Slides it back into the envelope.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_6.text: That's fine. Just make sure your critique only covers what you actually read.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_8.text: I sent it to publishers three times, and it was rejected all three times. What I needed wasn't vague encouragement, but to know where people stopped reading.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_9.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_9.text: *The mark left by a return sticker on the corner of the envelope catches my eye.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_10.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_10.text: I needed proof that someone had read it more than I needed praise. If I put that pressure on you, that's my fault as your teacher.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_11.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_11.text: Go on. You'll be late for the event.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_12.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_12.text: *I left and closed the classroom door. The envelope is still on the teacher's desk. A return-label mark the size of a fingernail remains on the surface.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_1.text: *The end of the paper bends slightly in her hand. Lips pressed together, she carefully smooths the folded edge.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_3.text: Yes. I don't want to just say something.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_5.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_5.text: *When I open the envelope, the smell of paper rises. The end of the last page is blank. Beneath a sentence crossed out in red, traces of starting again and stopping overlap.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_7.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_7.text: My hand stops whenever I look at the last page. It has for years.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_8.text: *She points to the final line with one fingertip. When the event announcement outside ends, only the sound of turning pages remains.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_9.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_9.text: Can I mark why I stopped on the last page?

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_11.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_11.text: Yes. I'm reading it as one of your readers.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_12.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_12.text: *She sets the clipboard on the desk and caps the red pen.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_13.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_13.text: All right. Put it in the anonymous feedback section.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_14.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_14.text: *She takes back the critique copy and rubs the old return-label mark on the envelope once with her thumb.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6.text: This is your copy number. I'll collect it with the others on Monday.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_b.text: *I remember the stack of critique copies at the café yesterday. The envelope is marked No. 04.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_d.text: Be honest, but only about as far as you read. You don't have to put your name on it.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_f.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_f.text: And don't try to figure out who wrote each comment.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_g.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_g.text: *She checks the number on the critique copy and nods.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_h.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_h.text: I never thought the day would come when I was ready to hear what people think.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_j.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_j.text: Just finish it before literature club on Monday.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_m.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_m.text: *She tucks a loose strand of hair behind her ear.* I don't accept book reports.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_o.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_o.text: *The corner of her mouth rises.* Right. Write at least one line.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_r.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_r.text: I'll take your answer at literature club on Monday. Until then, I'll keep working on the ending too.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_s.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_s.text: Now neither of us has an excuse.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_t.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_t.text: *She writes the critique deadline beneath the literature club schedule.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_7.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_7.text: That's enough thank-yous. Go help set up the event.

hidden_homeroom_d5_7_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_7_c.text: Focus on getting through the event. I'll see you at literature club on Monday.

hidden_homeroom_d5_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_8.text: *She steps into the hall and checks the names of the students preparing for the event.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.text: *She points to critique copy No. 04.* It's the final review. Don't go easy on it just because you see blanks.

hidden_nurse_d5_check.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_check.text: *During a break in the event, I pass the nurse's office.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1.text: Oh, {name}. Last day of the event. Let's close out your counseling record today too.

hidden_nurse_d5_1_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_b.text: *The nurse opens the final check box on the counseling form.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1_c.text: Once we check how you're doing today, this round of counseling is complete.

hidden_nurse_d5_1_d.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_d.text: So I don't have to come anymore?

hidden_nurse_d5_1_e.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1_e.text: If you're hurt or overwhelmed, come through the proper channel. You don't need to invent a reason.

hidden_nurse_d5_1_f.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_f.text: *Beneath the counseling form, the booking instructions for the nurse's office and school counseling center are printed side by side.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3.text: I'm here to pick up my counseling confirmation.

hidden_nurse_d5_3_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_3_b.text: *She writes the date and time on the form.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_3_c.text: You're always welcome to come for help at a scheduled time.

hidden_nurse_d5_3_f.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_3_f.text: *She opens a box of first-aid information cards.*

hidden_nurse_d5_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_4.text: The event first-aid kit is by the gym entrance. If anyone gets hurt, call the teacher in charge right away.

hidden_nurse_d5_4_c.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_4_c.text: *A stamp appears at the bottom of the form: 'Counseling concluded; rebook if needed.'*

hidden_nurse_d5_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_5.text: {name}. Want to take a first-aid information card?

hidden_nurse_d5_choice.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice.text: *The front lists basic first-aid steps; the back lists the school's counseling channels.*
choices: Yes. I'll keep it in my bag.
I'd rather know how to book the counseling center.
With this card, I won't need to go all the way to the counseling office.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a.text: *She slips the information card into a clear case and hands it to me.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a_b.text: The best outcome is never needing it. But if you do, take it out right away.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b.text: Good. If you book through the school app, a counselor can follow up even if I can't respond right away.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_b.text: *She points to the QR code on the back of the card.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_c.text: Tap 'Book Counseling' in the school app. You can choose the nurse's office or the school counseling center.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_d.text: If I can't answer right away, a counselor will take over. The record stays within the school.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_e.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_e.text: *Instead of a personal number, it lists available counseling hours and the departments in charge.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_f.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_f.text: If it were urgent, who would you tell first?

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_g.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_g.text: A parent, guardian, or a teacher I trust. I won't try to endure it alone.

hidden_nurse_d5_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_6.text: Then we're good. Here's the first-aid card.

hidden_nurse_d5_6_c.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_6_c.text: *A short line is printed at the bottom of the card: 'Ask for help before you get hurt.'*

hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.text: *She files the counseling form.* That's all for counseling. Next time, say what you need right away.

morning5_end.name: {name}
morning5_end.text: *I gather the notes on my desk, then check the notifications on my phone one by one.*

morning5_committed_end.name: {name}
morning5_committed_end.text: *I organize the notes on my desk and check the event schedule for the direction I've already chosen.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_trap.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_trap.text: It's the other way around. This card isn't for handling everything alone.

morning5_after_counteroffer.name: {name}
morning5_after_counteroffer.text: *A morning notice slides off the desk. No one picks it up. Before anyone can, an announcement about the event fills the classroom.*

morning5_sojeong_1.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_1.text: *I open my notes: unfinished attempts to report what happened to Sojeong, apologies written and erased. Draft thirty-nine is still blank.*

morning5_sojeong_2.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_2.text: *I do not start draft forty. I copy my apology into the chat and press send.*

morning5_sojeong_3.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_3.text: I saw what they did to your desk and the writing on it, but I never told a teacher. Looking away was my choice too. I'm sorry. You don't have to reply.

morning5_sojeong_4.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_4.text: *The sent indicator appears. I close the chat without waiting for a read receipt.*

morning5_sojeong_5.name: {name}
morning5_sojeong_5.text: *I message my current homeroom teacher too: 'I need to talk about something I chose to ignore at my old school.' I leave both messages on the screen until the festival announcement begins.*

morning5_caught_fallout_1.name: {name}
morning5_caught_fallout_1.text: *Before the event begins, the three of them sit far apart in the classroom. The duty sheet on the desk lists only the work that must be done.*

morning5_caught_fallout_2.name: {name}
morning5_caught_fallout_2.text: *Yuna leaves first with the guidebooks, and Dain takes the opposite door. Seoyeon picks up the attendance sheet without looking my way.*

morning5_caught_fallout_3.name: {name}
morning5_caught_fallout_3.text: *Until the event ends, the only words we exchange are work checks. At the final bell, they take three different staircases.*

morning5_harem_fallout_1.name: {name}
morning5_harem_fallout_1.text: *During the event, the three of them leave only necessary messages in the group chat. None of the private chats receive anything new.*

morning5_harem_fallout_2.name: Dain
morning5_harem_fallout_2.text: Even after this is over, let's not meet separately. Keep what we agreed on.

morning5_harem_fallout_3.name: {name}
morning5_harem_fallout_3.text: *I nod. The three of them leave through the school gate together, and I follow alone a little later.*

morning5_counteroffer_choice.name: {name}
morning5_counteroffer_choice.text: *When the conversation ends, both of them wait for an answer.*
choices: Answer the person I promised first and take responsibility
Say that I choose the person I went to last night
Let neither of them wait and end both relationships

morning5_counteroffer_choice_lead.name: {name}
morning5_counteroffer_choice_lead.text: *I turn toward the person I made the first promise to.* I will start by apologizing for what I chose last night. I will not ask you to hold on to me.

morning5_counteroffer_choice_tempter.name: {name}
morning5_counteroffer_choice_tempter.text: *I look at the person I went to last night, then bow to the other.* I will not hide where my feelings lean now. But I will not hold on to both of you.

morning5_counteroffer_choice_neither.name: {name}
morning5_counteroffer_choice_neither.text: *I take one step back from both of them.* I do not deserve to choose either of you right now. I will not hold on to either of you.
